title: Ang 762–763: the unskilled bride
hook: Guru Nanak's poems of the unskilled and the skilled bride
tomorrow: what does a house feel like when the one you waited for walks in?

segments.voice: Yesterday, ang 751: safflower's bright color lasts only a few days; the color that holds is soaked in deep. The bride. Today, a bride who says she has no skill at all.

The group project where everyone else seems to know what they're doing. The family kitchen where you're the one who can't cook. Feeling clumsy is its own kind of lonely. Guru Nanak wrote a poem in that voice. On ang 762, Kuchajji, the unskilled bride, begins, in paraphrase: I have no skill, my faults overflow; how can I go to my Husband?
screen: `EVERYONE ELSE KNOWS HOW.` → `I HAVE NO SKILL.` → `HOW CAN I GO TO HIM?`

segments.voice: Kuchajji stays honest all the way through. In paraphrase: the others each rise above one another; who would even know my name? She doesn't fake it. Right after her, on the same page, comes Suchajji, the skilled bride, and her skill isn't what you'd expect. No technique, no polish. In paraphrase: when you are with me, I have everyone; you, Master, are my wealth. Within you I live at peace. By your will a throne; by your will a beggar's road. Her skill is belonging, and she takes the throne and the road alike. Then, on ang 763, Guru Arjan adds Gunvanti, the virtuous bride, and her virtue is plain: whenever I see a Sikh of the Guru, I bow, again and again, at their feet. Read in order, the three poems answer the clumsy feeling. Clumsy doesn't shut you out; Kuchajji is in the Granth, saying it out loud. And the skill isn't a performance. It's being with the One, and bowing to the people around you. Skill in love.
screen: `KUCHAJJI: WHO WOULD KNOW MY NAME?` · `SUCHAJJI: WHEN YOU ARE, I HAVE ALL.` · `GUNVANTI: I BOW AT THEIR FEET.` · `CLUMSY DOESN'T SHUT YOU OUT.` · then, large: `SKILL IN LOVE.`

segments.voice: Count on your fingers, slowly, things you've been given that no skill of yours earned: a friend's patience, a meal, a second chance. One finger for each breath. When you run out of fingers, rest your hands open on your knees.
Ang 762. Where Guru Nanak's Kuchajji and Suchajji sit side by side: the unskilled bride and the skilled one.
Skill in love: not polish, but being there, and bowing to whoever's beside you. That's fifteen thirty-eight, clumsy and counted.

fork.setup: a new coworker keeps making mistakes and apologizing. a teammate says she just isn't good enough for the job. what fits ang 762?
options: agree; skill is what earns someone a place on a team.
tell her to stop apologizing and fake confidence instead.
clumsy doesn't shut anyone out; help her, and bow a little yourself.
fork.reveal: Kuchajji's honesty is kept in the Granth, Suchajji's skill is belonging, and Gunvanti's virtue is bowing to others.

original.note: Gurmukhi: Kuchaji, the unskilled one; its partner poem is Suchaji, the skilled one (ang 762).
